notable_absence.finding: This page's next-steps SDK list ('.NET | Go | Java | Kotlin | Node.js | PHP | Python | Ruby | Scala') links out to nine separate SDK full-text-search howto pages, none of which have any extraction-layer id yet in this registry under any namespace searched (sdk:, fts:, search:) - a large, entirely unextracted fan-out from this one page that no round in this project appears to have touched yet.

cross_component_finding: This REST reference page demonstrates two advanced index-configuration features inline, as full worked JSON examples, that create-search-index-ui.md (this batch, the paired UI page for the identical task) does not mention at all: a dynamic XATTRs mapping (availableSince 7.6.2) and a custom document filter using a conjunct filter (availableSince 8.0, Couchbase Server 8.0 marker). create-search-index-ui.md instead explicitly scopes itself to a 'basic index' and defers ALL customization, including presumably these same two features, to a separate page, [Customize a Search Index with the Web Console](customize-index.md), which is outside this batch. So the REST/UI content gap here is not a real capability difference (the UI can plausibly reach the same JSON structure through Customize a Search Index) but it is a real documentation-scope difference: the REST page teaches these two advanced features directly as part of 'how to create an index', while the UI-facing task page teaches only the minimal path and pushes everything else one hop further away. Flagging since it affects how discoverable these two version-gated features are depending on which of the two paired pages a reader lands on first.
